title: Genomic REML without forming the covariance matrix
text: Simulated genotypes 1,500 individuals four subpopulations, 3,000 markers, trait heritability 0.5: history records iteration’s estimates, trace estimate, standard error trace estimate, measures far randomized fit can sit exact one:  exact fit, comparison: two estimates h2h^2 differ 0.13 exact standard errors: error sketch adds small next sampling error REML . solve took 8.4 conjugate gradient iterations average. spectrum GG shows needed:  Population structure puts 3 eigenvalues far rest, rank-100 preconditioner removes. ideal rank-100 preconditioner maps top 100 eigenvalues G+μIG + \mu λ100+μ\lambda_{100} + \mu leaves others alone, preconditioned system condition number (λ100+μ)/μ=3.7(\lambda_{100} + \mu)/\mu = 3.7, μ=0.84\mu = 0.84. condition number conjugate gradients need iterations.
code: library(matsketch) set.seed(11) dat <- sim_genomic(n = 1500, p = 3000, h2 = 0.5, pops = 4) G <- grm_matrix(dat$M) fit <- reml_sketch(dat$y, G) fit #> <reml_sketch> converged in 4 iterations (rpchol rank-100 preconditioner, XTrace with 40 products) #>          estimate std.error #> genetic    0.5212    0.0546 #> residual   0.4375    0.0404 #> h2         0.5436    0.0454 #>   linear systems solved : 180 (mean 8.4 CG iterations) fit$history #>   iteration   genetic  residual trace_PG trace_se       change #> 1         1 0.5248868 0.4325594 1302.709 4.328189 1.187296e-01 #> 2         2 0.5211177 0.4375674 1333.567 4.193366 1.157773e-02 #> 3         3 0.5212062 0.4375185 1331.921 4.211137 1.698354e-04 #> 4         4 0.5212044 0.4375233 1331.864 4.210621 1.093405e-05 plot(fit) exact <- reml_exact(dat$y, as.matrix(G)) rbind(sketched = c(fit$sigma2, h2 = fit$h2, se_h2 = fit$se[["h2"]]),       exact = c(exact$sigma2, h2 = exact$h2, se_h2 = exact$se[["h2"]])) #>            genetic  residual        h2      se_h2 #> sketched 0.5212044 0.4375233 0.5436418 0.04541329 #> exact    0.5279405 0.4326637 0.5495922 0.04517044 ev <- eigen(as.matrix(G), symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values mu <- fit$sigma2[["residual"]] / fit$sigma2[["genetic"]] keep <- ev > 1e-8 plot(which(keep), ev[keep], log = "y", pch = 19, cex = 0.4, col = "#0072B2",      xlab = "index", ylab = "eigenvalue of G") abline(v = 100.5, lty = 2, col = "grey50") abline(h = mu, lty = 3, lwd = 2, col = "#D55E00") legend("topright", c("preconditioner rank", "mu at the estimate"),        lty = c(2, 3), lwd = c(1, 2), col = c("grey50", "#D55E00"),        bty = "n")

code: sc <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "reml-scaling.csv",                            package = "matsketch")) secs <- with(sc, tapply(seconds, list(n, method), sum)) secs <- secs[, c("form_G", "exact", "eigen", "sketch_dense", "sketch_lazy")] round(secs, 1) #>       form_G exact eigen sketch_dense sketch_lazy #> 1000     2.8   1.6   0.7          1.2        10.1 #> 2000    11.8  12.0   6.0          4.2        20.9 #> 4000    48.3 114.9  49.2         17.8        48.8 #> 8000   193.0 848.1    NA         69.5        96.1 #> 16000     NA    NA    NA           NA       251.9 tot <- cbind(   `exact REML` = secs[, "form_G"] + secs[, "exact"],   `eigendecomposition only` = secs[, "form_G"] + secs[, "eigen"],   `sketch, G formed` = secs[, "form_G"] + secs[, "sketch_dense"],   `sketch, grm_matrix()` = secs[, "sketch_lazy"] ) n <- as.numeric(rownames(secs)) cols <- c("#999999", "#0072B2", "#E69F00", "#D55E00") matplot(n, tot / 60, log = "xy", type = "b", pch = 19, lty = 1, lwd = 2,         col = cols, xlab = "individuals", ylab = "minutes") legend("topleft", colnames(tot), col = cols, lwd = 2, pch = 19, bty = "n") mem <- with(sc[sc$method %in% c("exact", "sketch_dense", "sketch_lazy"), ],             tapply(memory_gb, list(n, method), sum)) round(mem, 2) #>       exact sketch_dense sketch_lazy #> 1000   0.03         0.01        0.04 #> 2000   0.12         0.03        0.07 #> 4000   0.48         0.12        0.15 #> 8000   1.91         0.48        0.30 #> 16000    NA           NA        0.60

title: Randomized matrix computations with matsketch
text: Nyström approximation rebuilds positive-semidefinite matrix AA subset SS columns, ̂=:,SAS,S+,:\hat = A_{:,S}\, A_{S,S}^{+}\, A_{S,:}, everything depends columns chosen. Randomly pivoted Cholesky (Chen, Epperly, Tropp Webber, 2025) chooses one time, probability proportional diagonal part AA yet explained. Greedy pivoting, classical rule, always takes largest residual instead, uniform sampling ignores matrix altogether. points form large cluster, small cluster scatter outliers, layout defeats classical rules. kernel_matrix() stores points computes entries algorithm asks . rule gets budget 100 columns, trace_path records error every pivot, one fit per rule traces whole curve. best possible error rank comes eigenvalues, small example lets us compute:  Randomly pivoted Cholesky stays within small factor best possible error every rank. Greedy pivoting falls far behind first, spends early pivots outliers isolated points edges clusters, explains little beyond ; catches working . Uniform sampling keeps pace early stalls. almost never draws outlier, every outlier misses leaves whole diagonal entry unexplained: 20 outliers hold 1.3% trace, error levels . first 40 pivots rule show budget goes:  three rules read small share matrix; differ entries read. default method = "accelerated" draws pivots distribution one---time random pivoting proposes blocks accepts rejection sampling (Epperly, Tropp Webber, 2025), work matrix-matrix arithmetic.
code: set.seed(1) X <- rbind(   matrix(rnorm(2 * 1300, sd = 0.5), ncol = 2),     # large cluster   matrix(rnorm(2 * 180, sd = 0.2), ncol = 2) + 4,  # small cluster   matrix(runif(2 * 20, -6, 10), ncol = 2)          # outliers ) K <- kernel_matrix(X, "gaussian", bandwidth = 0.5) K #> <matsketch_kernel> gaussian kernel on 1500 points, bandwidth 0.5 #>   full matrix would hold 2,250,000 entries; nothing is stored rules <- c(rpchol = "accelerated", greedy = "greedy", uniform = "uniform") fits <- lapply(rules, function(r) rpchol(K, k = 100, method = r)) ev <- eigen(as.matrix(K), symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values best <- 1 - cumsum(ev[1:100]) / sum(ev)  ranks <- c(20, 40, 100) tab <- cbind(sapply(fits, function(f) f$trace_path[ranks]), best = best[ranks]) rownames(tab) <- paste("rank", ranks) signif(tab, 2) #>           rpchol  greedy uniform    best #> rank 20  0.12000 0.67000   0.190 4.4e-02 #> rank 40  0.03200 0.18000   0.041 1.4e-02 #> rank 100 0.00025 0.00032   0.015 4.3e-05 cols <- c(rpchol = "#D55E00", greedy = "#0072B2", uniform = "#E69F00") plot(best, log = "y", type = "l", lwd = 2, lty = 2, col = "grey30",      ylim = range(best, unlist(lapply(fits, `[[`, "trace_path"))),      xlab = "rank", ylab = "relative trace error") for (r in names(fits)) lines(fits[[r]]$trace_path, lwd = 2, col = cols[[r]]) legend("topright", c(names(fits), "best possible"), col = c(cols, "grey30"),        lty = c(1, 1, 1, 2), lwd = 2, bty = "n") op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 2, 0.5)) for (r in names(fits)) {   plot(X, pch = 16, cex = 0.35, col = "grey75", asp = 1, axes = FALSE,        xlab = "", ylab = "", main = r)   points(X[fits[[r]]$pivots[1:40], ], pch = 16, cex = 0.7, col = "#D55E00")   box(col = "grey85") } par(op) sapply(fits, function(f) f$entries / K$n^2) #>     rpchol     greedy    uniform  #> 0.06795556 0.06733333 0.06733333

what: Estimating a trace from matrix-vector products
title: Randomized matrix computations with matsketch
text: Traces matrices expensive form everywhere: effective degrees freedom smoother, derivative log-determinant, score equations REML. Girard-Hutchinson estimator averages ω⊤Aω\omega^\top \omega random vectors ω\omega needs products AA, error falls like 1/m1/\sqrt{m} number products mm. Hutch++ (Meyer, Musco, Musco Woodruff, 2021) first removes low-rank approximation AA estimates left. XTrace (Epperly, Tropp Webber, 2024) , uses every product jobs leave-one-construction, XNysTrace counterpart positive-semidefinite matrices. test matrix eigenvalues 1,1/4,1/9,…1, 1/4, 1/9, \dots: XTrace reports standard error spread leave-one-estimates. median relative error estimator ten repetitions, budget products grows:  Girard-Hutchinson line slope −1/2-1/2; others fall far faster, extra product also sharpens low-rank part. diag_est() applies construction diagonal:
code: set.seed(2) n <- 500 U <- qr.Q(qr(matrix(rnorm(n * n), n))) A <- U %*% ((1:n)^-2 * t(U)) trA <- sum(diag(A)) trA #> [1] 1.642936 trace_est(A, m = 60) #> <trace_est> xtrace, 60 matrix-vector products #>   estimate       : 1.64281 #>   standard error : 0.001416 budgets <- c(12, 24, 48, 96, 192) methods <- c(hutchinson = "#999999", hutchpp = "#E69F00",              xtrace = "#D55E00", xnystrace = "#0072B2") err <- sapply(names(methods), function(meth) {   sapply(budgets, function(m) {     median(replicate(10, abs(trace_est(A, m, meth)$estimate - trA) / trA))   }) }) matplot(budgets, err, log = "xy", type = "b", pch = 19, lty = 1, lwd = 2,         col = methods, xlab = "matrix-vector products",         ylab = "relative error") legend("bottomleft", names(methods), col = methods, lwd = 2, pch = 19,        bty = "n") cor(diag_est(A, m = 100), diag(A)) #> [1] 0.9999593

text: Systems (K+μI)x=b(K + \mu ) x = b arise kernel ridge regression, Gaussian-process prediction, every step REML fit. Conjugate gradients need products KK, μ\mu small need many . Frangella, Tropp Udell (2023) precondition low-rank approximation K≈UΛ̂U⊤K \approx U \hat\Lambda U^\top, show rank three times effective dimension deff(μ)=tr{K(K+μI)−1}d_{\mathrm{eff}}(\mu) = \mathrm{tr}\{K (K + \mu )^{-1}\} keeps iteration count small regardless nn. effective_dim() estimates deffd_{\mathrm{eff}} low-rank approximation returns recommended rank: estimate rank-200 approximation already asks rank 200, preconditioner built recommended rank. comparison, preconditioner rank 50 preconditioner :  Even rank 50 cuts count 1232 iterations 171. recommended rank approximation captures nearly matrix level μ\mu, preconditioned system well conditioned 2 iterations enough. preconditioner depends μ\mu diagonal, one approximation serves every value μ\mu application visits. pcg() also accepts matrix right-hand sides advances together, turns step one matrix-matrix product.
code: set.seed(3) Z <- matrix(rnorm(3 * 1000), ncol = 3) K2 <- as.matrix(kernel_matrix(Z, "gaussian", bandwidth = 2)) b <- rnorm(1000) mu <- 1e-4  ed <- effective_dim(rpchol(K2, k = 200), mu) ed #> $d_eff #> [1] 122.2534 #>  #> $recommended_rank #> [1] 369 #>  #> $sufficient #> [1] FALSE precond_of_rank <- function(k) nystrom_precond(rpchol(K2, k), mu) runs <- list(   plain = pcg(K2, b, mu = mu, maxit = 5000),   `rank 50` = pcg(K2, b, mu = mu, precond = precond_of_rank(50)),   recommended = pcg(K2, b, mu = mu,                     precond = precond_of_rank(ed$recommended_rank)) ) sapply(runs, `[[`, "iterations") #>       plain     rank 50 recommended  #>        1232         171           2 cols <- c("#999999", "#E69F00", "#D55E00") plot(runs$plain$residuals, log = "y", type = "l", lwd = 2, col = cols[1],      xlab = "iteration", ylab = "relative residual") for (i in 2:3) {   lines(runs[[i]]$residuals, type = "o", pch = 19, cex = 0.4, lwd = 2,         col = cols[i]) } legend("topright", names(runs), col = cols, lwd = 2, bty = "n")

text: matsketch answers questions large positive-semidefinite matrix, kernel matrix, genomic relationship matrix covariance matrix, reading small part . implements recent randomized algorithms numerical linear algebra R implementation: rpchol(): randomly pivoted Cholesky, builds near-optimal low-rank approximation (k+1)n(k + 1)n matrix’s n2n^2 entries (Chen, Epperly, Tropp Webber, 2025), accelerated rejection-sampling variant (Epperly, Tropp Webber, 2025). trace_est() diag_est(): XTrace, XNysTrace XDiag estimators, recover trace diagonal matrix-vector products (Epperly, Tropp Webber, 2024), Hutch++ Girard-Hutchinson comparison. nystrom_precond() pcg(): randomized Nyström preconditioning conjugate gradients (Frangella, Tropp Udell, 2023). reml_sketch(): three combined REML genomic variance components never forms covariance matrix, grm_matrix() never forms relationship matrix either. estimator tested brute-force version definition.

code: set.seed(1) U <- qr.Q(qr(matrix(rnorm(300 * 300), 300))) A <- U %*% diag((1:300)^-2) %*% t(U) sum(diag(A)) #> [1] 1.641606 trace_est(A, m = 40) #> <trace_est> xtrace, 40 matrix-vector products #>   estimate       : 1.63371 #>   standard error : 0.002271 trace_est(A, m = 40, method = "hutchinson") #> <trace_est> hutchinson, 40 matrix-vector products #>   estimate       : 1.62383 #>   standard error : 0.208

title: matsketch 0.1.0
text: First release. rpchol(): randomly pivoted Cholesky, simple accelerated (rejection-sampling) forms, greedy uniform pivoting baselines. trace_est() diag_est(): XTrace, XNysTrace XDiag estimators, Hutch++ Girard-Hutchinson comparison. nystrom(), nystrom_precond(), effective_dim() pcg(): randomized Nystrom preconditioning conjugate gradients, solving many right-hand sides . reml_sketch() reml_exact(): variance components average-information REML, covariance matrix never formed sketched fit. kernel_matrix() grm_matrix(): kernel genomic relationship matrices evaluated needed.
